name: Barth Hotel
headline: Eaton Senior Communities plans to buy and fully renovate the vacant, landmarked Barth Hotel in Lower Downtown Denver into 50 studio apartments for seniors 62+ earning 30% to 50% AMI, and won 2026 Round One federal 9%, state and TOC credits from CHFA.
why_it_matters: It shows how an old affordability covenant on a building can keep a prime downtown site in senior housing: the covenant held the purchase price down, and a new Downtown Development Authority loan helped fill the gap. The deal still has to close by 2026-12-31 or the building goes to a hotelier.

status.label: Credits awarded; purchase closing not confirmed
status.detail: CHFA lists the award as of 2026-09-30, and BusinessDen reported the award in May 2026. Eaton must close on the building by 2026-12-31, or the hotel option passes to Sage Hospitality. There is no public record of the closing, a building permit or a construction start. Construction is expected in 2027.

next_step: Watch for a recorded deed or covenant amendment for 1514 17th St. (Denver Clerk and Recorder) and the financing closing before 2026-12-31. Without that closing the agreed fallback to the hotel plan takes effect.

key_numbers.meaning: Independent living for seniors 62+ at 30% to 50% AMI, cut down from a 62-unit former rooming house and assisted living building.
About $14.5M over the 10-year credit period, plus $500,000 state credit and $100,000 TOC credit.
A low-interest loan from the Denver Downtown Development Authority, approved 2026-01-27. It may shrink to about $4M if historic tax credits come through.
That is the city staff estimate as the Gazette reported it. The applicant says the credit ask is about $200,000 per unit, well below new construction.

background.text: Opened in 1882 as a liquor wholesaler's warehouse, it soon became a hotel, last known as Hotel Barth. It was converted to housing around 1980.

Senior Housing Options ran it as a room-and-board SRO and later as a Medicaid-funded assisted living facility. The owner moved residents out by December 2024 after the elevator failed and listed the 62-unit building for sale. The listing broker estimated it needs at least $10M of work.

Earlier CHFA, CDOH and City of Denver funding left affordability covenants on the property. The Gazette describes a 60-year affordable housing covenant. The applicant says these covenants keep the purchase price well below market.
In September 2025 the CEO of Sage Hospitality was under contract to buy the Barth and turn it back into a hotel, which would require lifting the covenants. City Council members raised concerns.
In early 2026 the two sides agreed that Eaton has until 2026-12-31 to buy the building. If it does not close by then, the hotelier gets his chance at a 40-room hotel.
Eaton has site control through an executed purchase and sale agreement. The purchase price is not public; the building was listed for $2.5M in 2025.

Rehab scope: full interior gut with the historic lobby and corridors kept. Units are enlarged so each has a bathroom and galley kitchen. All MEP is replaced, with heat pumps and cooling, and the building goes all-electric. Work adds a new 5-stop stretcher-size elevator plus a LULA to the basement, an NFPA 13 sprinkler system, new electrical service and refurbished historic windows. It follows Enterprise Green Communities.
CHFA granted a waiver so the units need no dishwashers, because the historic layout limits space.
Ground floor: lobby and amenity space, service offices, a food pantry with cold storage, a potluck kitchen and laundry. The mezzanine holds a library, exercise space and health and wellness rooms.
The applicant says the LoDo District and the LoDoNa registered neighborhood organization support the project.
At the December 2025 letter-of-intent stage CHFA coded the deal Older Adult, Veterans and acquisition/rehab. By the February 2026 application it was coded Older Adult and acquisition/rehab only.

discrepancies.text: Denver's DDDA release calls the $6M a low-interest loan, while the Denver Gazette says the board voted to grant $6 million.
CHFA and the city name the sponsor Eaton Senior Communities, Inc., while the Denver Gazette calls it Eaton Senior Services.

open_questions: Purchase price and closing date (the building was listed at $2.5M; the price under the executed PSA is not public).
Amounts of the CDOH soft loan, the existing HOST loan balance, permanent debt and historic tax credit equity, plus the lender and syndicator.
Terms of the city covenant/loan amendment that set the 2026-12-31 deadline. There is no public Denver Council record of it.
Length of the new CHFA affordability period (LURA).
Whether any project-based vouchers or rental subsidy apply. The CHFA reports show none.
